title: The night Madonna performed at the Haçienda for £50, then wiped it from her memory

input.lead: “I think she's a wonderful artist and I love the way she's so rude to people,” the late Tony Wilson once said of Madonna.
input.summary: “I think she's a wonderful artist and I love the way she's so rude to people,” the late Tony Wilson once said of Madonna. And he should know The Factory Records boss had first-hand experience with the pop superstar’s brusque manner after she performed at the Haçienda in 1984 for
input.evidence_text: “I think she's a wonderful artist and I love the way she's so rude to people,” the late Tony Wilson once said of Madonna. And he should know The Factory Records boss had first-hand experience with the pop superstar’s brusque manner after she performed at the Haçienda in 1984 for the princely sum of £50 The bargain price gig was negotiated by television executive Malcolm Gerrie, who persuaded Madonna's record company to organise her appearance at the venue as part of a one-off, live Channel 4 broadcast of cult music show The Tube View 4 Images Madonna performing at The Hacienda, Manchester, on an episode of The Tube (Image: Channel 4/The Tube/YouTube screengrab) Free ticket-holders to the Haçienda showcase on January 27, 1984 were there to see the Factory Allstars - a band pulled together for the night by members of Durutti Column, A Certain Ratio, Quando Quango and soul singer Marcel King. input.evidence_text: New Manchester research suggests tackling the factors behind suspensions could help prevent repeated exclusions and support vulnerable pupils School suspensions are associated with a complex combination of socioeconomic disadvantage, special educational needs, peer relationships and pupils’ experiences of school, according to new research from The University of Manchester The study analysed survey responses from more than 19,000 secondary school pupils linked to administrative records across Hampshire & Isle of Wight, to examine a wide range of factors associated with whether pupils were suspended and how often suspensions occurred Researchers found pupils receiving special educational needs (SEN) support or with an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) were more than twice as likely to be suspended than pupils without SEN, while those eligible for free school meals were also at increased risk The analysis also identified a number of factors associated with lower suspension risk, including pupils feeling that they belonged at school, being satisfied with their academic attainment, having positive relationships with school staff and having stronger emotion regulation sk By contrast, higher levels of peer pressure, experiences of bullying, and recent substance use were associated with an increased likelihood of suspension

From the streets of New Jersey to the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, this is the musical that’s too good to be true. They were just four guys from Jersey, until they sang their very first note. They had a sound nobody had ever heard… and the radio just couldn’t get enough of. But while their harmonies were perfect on stage, off stage it was a very different story -- a story that has made them an international sensation all over again. The show features all their hits including “Sherry,” “Big Girls Don’t Cry,” “Walk Like A Man,” “Can’t Take My Eyes Off You,” “Beggin’,” “December 1963 (Oh What a Night)” and more. input.evidence_text: Events EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters Official Chamber Post FREE Online Thursday 10 Sep 10am - 11am Book Now About the event The way low-value goods enter the European Union is changing From 1 July 2026, the EU introduced a new €3 customs duty on low-value consignments valued up to €150 entering the EU from outside the bloc. The change removes the previous duty exemption and introduces new considerations for businesses exporting goods directly to EU customers The new duty applies based on product categories/tariff classifications rather than simply per parcel, meaning shipments containing different types of goods could face multiple charges. For example, a parcel containing products under different tariff headings may attract multiple While the change is aimed largely at addressing the growth of low-value e-commerce imports, it will also impact UK businesses selling products directly into EU markets, including online retailers, brands and SMEs What the new €3 EU customs duty means for UK businesses
